job: Make the project and FastAPI material budgets price glazing from the design's measured glazed area and doors from the design's door count, while preserving the existing Alberta reference band as a visibly derived proxy rather than inventing a local quote.

inputs.evidence: The only checked-in glazing anchor is CAD 900–1,800 per triple-pane window. No separate per-square-foot supplier quote is registered.

outputs.acceptance: Equal glazed area produces equal glazing cost regardless of opening count; greater area produces proportionally greater proxy cost; the visible basis discloses the source band, reference-size divisor, limitations and date.
Project budgets use the exterior-door count drawn by the design; a zero-door dwelling carries one explicitly disclosed entry-door allowance rather than a silent constant.
The TypeScript app and FastAPI materials engine use the same quantities, rates, rounding semantics and limitation wording for a shared fixture.
Focused budget, copilot, API-parity, TypeScript and registered full-suite gates pass from an isolated committed snapshot.

dependsOn.evidence: BuildingGraph and legacy builder documents already expose glazed area and opening kinds to the project budget on origin/main d0fc2f6.
ProjectBudget already binds design hash, scenario, region, source references and date; BQ02 repairs one quantity/basis mismatch without claiming quote fidelity.

rejectionGates: Reject if any landing-scene, Three.js, animation, model, meadow, tree, sky, mountain, shader, camera, lighting, builder plan geometry, GLB or generated-plan asset changes.
Reject if CAD 900–1,800 per window is presented as a separately sourced per-square-foot rate, local quote, supplier offer or construction take-off.
Reject if the reference-size divisor is justified by an uncommitted or frozen plan-catalog expansion.

Reject if a glazing count is multiplied by price, if project or FastAPI budgets retain a silent hardcoded door quantity, or if app and FastAPI engines disagree on a shared fixture. A frozen legacy catalog caller may retain the old two-door allowance only when its basis explicitly says the design count is unavailable.
Reject if the pricing basis claims that NBC 9.36 compliance was checked by the budget function.
Reject if the existing Alberta cost-model numbers change, if unsupported-region pricing is introduced, or if any external supplier, legal, payment, HOMES, deployment or outreach gate is crossed.
Reject if any new test is absent from a declared test gate or if published gate counts change without a complete runner observation.

verify.freshContextVerifier: A verifier that did not implement BQ02 must inspect the final stable snapshot when delegation is authorized.
commands: cd app && npx playwright test tests/glazing-area-pricing.spec.ts tests/project-budget.spec.ts tests/copilot.spec.ts tests/gate-coverage.spec.ts --workers=1
anchors: One opening at 306 square feet costs more than one opening at 16 square feet under the disclosed proxy.
The same glazed area split across one or four openings has the same proxy price.
Two doors retain the old two-door allowance exactly; one or three doors use their actual quantities.
TypeScript and Python return matching glazing and door lines for the same fixture.
No changed path is under the frozen 3D, animation, model or plan-geometry sets.

repair.scope: Only BQ02 quantity, basis, parity or test-gate integration may be repaired. A second failure returns the node to blocked without touching any frozen visual path.
